---
name: replan-step
description: "Re-plan a PLAN.md step the executor escalated ([?]) or failed ([!]), then hand it back"
---
A step of `PLAN.md` came back from the executor: it escalated the step (marked `[?]` with an `- Escalation:` note) or failed it (marked `[!]`).

Step and details (may be empty): the request given after the command name
If that is empty, take the first step marked `[?]` or `[!]`.

You are the planner. Do the deep reasoning the executor must not do, then hand the step back for execution.

1. Read `PLAN.md`, the step and its Escalation note, and the current state of the files it touches — `git status` and `git diff` show any partial work.
2. If the step failed, run its Done-when command and read the failure. When the Context for the executor has a `- Prelude:` line, run its command first in the same PowerShell, dot-sourced, as the executor does: `$global:LASTEXITCODE = 0; try { . <prelude> } catch { $_; "prelude failed"; exit 2 }; if (-not $? -or $LASTEXITCODE) { "prelude failed"; exit 2 }; <the Done-when command>`, where `<prelude>` is that line's command. When it exits 2 and the output's last line, apart from any exit code your shell adds, is `prelude failed`, the check never ran, and the step isn't what failed: stop, show me the prelude's error, and say to fix the `- prelude:` line in the `## Landing` section of `AGENTS.md`, or the script it names, and the plan's `- Prelude:` line. Leave the step as it is.
3. Decide why it came back, with evidence: the step was ambiguous, too big, wrong about the code, missing context, needs a redesign, or is beyond the executor model.
4. Fix the plan rather than the code:
   - Ambiguous or wrong about the code: rewrite the step with exact files, symbols and behavior.
   - Too big: split it into smaller steps and renumber the steps after it.
   - Missing context: add it to Context for the executor or to the step.
   - Needs a redesign: make the design decision, record it under Decisions, and update every later step it affects.
   - Beyond the executor model: implement only this step yourself, run its Done-when command, and mark it `[x]`.
5. Keep or revert the partial work deliberately — say which, and run `git checkout -- <files>` when reverting.
6. Remove the step's `- Escalation:` line (its outcome now lives in the step or under Decisions) and change the heading marker back from `[?]` or `[!]` to `[ ]`, unless you completed the step.
7. When `PLAN.md` has an `Issue:` line under its title and this re-plan changed the Decisions or added or removed steps, post a short comment on each issue on that line yourself, one comment per issue: `Re-plan of step N` and two to five lines on what changed and why, without the full plan. On GitHub run `gh issue comment <number> --body-file <file>`, with the text in a temporary file outside the repository; on GitLab (`git remote get-url origin` contains `gitlab`) run `glab issue note <number> --message <text>`. When posting fails, say so in your report. A re-plan that only rewords or clarifies a step posts nothing. On GitHub, a session's own GitHub tooling can add agent attribution to what it posts: a Claude Code cloud session appends a line `---` and then a footer line `_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/…)_` to each pull request description, issue, comment and review-thread reply it creates, through `gh` and the GitHub MCP tools alike, while `gh` in a local session appends nothing. So straight after each command that creates or edits a pull request description, an issue or a top-level comment, read back what was saved: `gh pr view <number> --json body --jq .body` for a pull request, `gh issue view <number> --json body --jq .body` for an issue, or `gh api "repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/comments/<id>" --jq .body` for a comment, where `<id>` is the number after `#issuecomment-` in the URL the command printed. When the last line of it that isn't blank starts with `Generated with [Claude Code` or `Generated by [Claude Code`, after any symbols or underscores, or holds only a `claude.ai/code/session_` link, remove that line, the `---` line above it, when there is one, and the blank lines between and after them, and keep every other line as it was. Remove it with the GitHub MCP tools, which don't append the footer again: `update_pull_request` with the new body for a pull request, `issue_write` with `method: update` and the new body for an issue, or `update_issue_comment` with the comment's id and the new body for a comment. Never remove it through `gh`: in such a session `gh api -X PATCH` appends the footer again. Then read it back once more, and when the footer is still there, or the GitHub MCP tools aren't available, leave it and list it in your report. A reply on a review thread is the one exception: nothing the session can call edits one without the footer, so post each reply as these instructions say anyway, because every finding still gets its reply, and list the replies in your report as ones that may carry the footer.
8. Report what changed and why, then hand the step back for execution. If `git log --oneline` already shows two "Re-plan step N" commits for this step, stop and ask me instead of re-planning a third time.
